mainTopic: How long the שעיר המשתלח must stay alive, and attempts to prove whether the הגרלה is מעכב
overview: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא on the פסוק 'יעמד חי לפני ה׳ לכפר עליו', which asks how long the goat for עזאזל must stay alive. רבי יהודה says it must stay alive until the blood of the other goat is applied. רבי שמעון says it must stay alive until the וידוי דברים. Their disagreement depends on the word 'לכפר': רבי יהודה reads it as כפרת דמים, and רבי שמעון reads it as כפרת דברים. The גמרא then tries to prove whether the הגרלה (the lottery) is מעכב. The first proof comes from a question asked to רבי עקיבא about a lot that came up in the left hand, but רבא shows the question was only about moving the lot and its goat to the right side. The second proof comes from a ברייתא on the word 'עלה', but רבא rereads it as saying only that the lot need not stay on the goat until שחיטה. A third source, 'ועשהו חטאת', teaches that only the גורל, and not a verbal naming, makes the goat a חטאת, even though a קל וחומר might suggest otherwise.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: The goat lives until the other goat's blood is applied
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק 'יעמד חי'. רבי יהודה rules that the שעיר המשתלח must stay alive until the blood of its partner goat is applied.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'It shall be stood alive before ה׳, to atone over it.' Until when must it stay alive? Until the time the blood of its partner goat is applied. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא asking how long the goat for עזאזל must stay alive, and gives רבי יהודה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'חי' (alive) tells us the goat must stay alive for a certain period. If it dies before then, a new one is needed. רבי יהודה sets the deadline at the moment the blood of the שעיר לה׳ is applied inside.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat sent away to עזאזל on יום כיפור
'Shall be stood alive': the goat must remain alive
Required, needs to
The application of its blood
Its partner, meaning the other goat (the שעיר לה׳)

steps.confusionAlert: 'חבירו' does not mean a friend. It means the partner goat, the שעיר לה׳ whose blood is sprinkled. The live goat itself has no blood applied.

phrases.english: "It shall be stood alive before ה׳, to atone over it"

phrases.aramaic: עַד מָתַי יִהְיֶה זָקוּק לַעֲמוֹד חַי?
phrases.english: Until when must it be required to stand alive?

phrases.aramaic: עַד שְׁעַת מַתַּן דָּמוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ —
phrases.english: Until the time of the application of the blood of its partner
phrases.notes: The partner is the שעיר לה׳.

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד מָתַי יִהְיֶה זָקוּק לַעֲמוֹד חַי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the שעיר המשתלח must stay alive until the blood of the שעיר לה׳ is applied.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: The goat lives until the spoken confession
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees with רבי יהודה. The goat must stay alive until the וידוי דברים is said over it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: until the time of the spoken confession.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי שמעון's opposing view on the goat's deadline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The וידוי over the live goat is said after the blood service is finished. So רבי שמעון requires the goat to stay alive longer than רבי יהודה does. The practical difference: if the goat dies between the blood and the וידוי, רבי יהודה needs no new goat, but רבי שמעון does.

keyTerms.meaning: A spoken confession: the כהן גדול confesses the people's sins over the goat

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a clear מחלוקת. The next steps explain the source of each opinion.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Until the time of the verbal confession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, the goat must stay alive until the וידוי דברים.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what lies at the base of the מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the two opinions. This is a setup line that prepares the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on either opinion. It is a request to find which reading of the פסוק leads each תנא to his view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'About what do they argue?' A request for the root of a מחלוקת

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind steps 1 and 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which point of interpretation separates רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבי יהודה reads 'to atone' as atonement through blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a ברייתא. רבי יהודה reads 'לכפר' as כפרת דמים and proves it from the פסוק 'וכלה מכפר את הקדש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: 'To atone' means the פסוק is speaking about atonement through blood. And the תורה similarly says: 'And when he finishes atoning for the קודש.' Just as there it means atonement through blood, so too here it means atonement through blood. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא. It begins with רבי יהודה's reading of the word 'לכפר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה links 'לכפר' in our פסוק to 'מכפר' in the later פסוק 'וכלה מכפר את הקדש'. That later פסוק clearly refers to the blood sprinklings. So the goat only needs to live until that blood atonement is finished, which explains his deadline in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As it was taught': introduces a ברייתא
Atonement achieved through sprinkling blood
'And similarly it says': brings a parallel פסוק
'Just as there, so too here': applies one פסוק's meaning to another

phrases.english: As it was taught: "To atone"
the verse speaks of atonement through blood,
and similarly it says:
"And when he finishes atoning for the Sanctuary"
Just as there it refers to atonement through blood,
so too here it refers to atonement through blood,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 by showing רבי יהודה's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה reads 'לכפר' as כפרת דמים, learned from 'וכלה מכפר את הקדש'.

steps.title: רבי שמעון reads 'to atone over it' as atonement through words
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון focuses on the word 'עליו' (over it). He reads 'לכפר עליו' as כפרת דברים, the וידוי said over the goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: 'To atone over it' means the פסוק is speaking about atonement through words.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by giving רבי שמעון's reading, which completes the answer to 'במאי קא מיפלגי'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'over it' point to atonement done on this goat itself. No blood is applied to the live goat, but the וידוי is said over it. So it must stay alive until the וידוי, which explains רבי שמעון's deadline in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: Atonement achieved through spoken words (the וידוי)
'Over it': the key word רבי שמעון focuses on

steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת comes down to the meaning of 'לכפר'. רבי יהודה says it means blood atonement, so the goat lives until the other goat's blood is applied. רבי שמעון says it means spoken atonement over this goat, so it lives until the וידוי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: "To atone over it",
the verse speaks of atonement through words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by giving the opposing reading to step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון reads 'לכפר עליו' as כפרת דברים, the וידוי said over the goat.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's students ask about a lot that came up in the left hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a 'תא שמע' about the lottery (הגרלה). It quotes a question put to רבי עקיבא: if the lot came up in the left hand, may the כהן גדול move it to the right?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי עקיבא's students asked him: if the lot came up in the left hand, may he move it back to the right hand?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to shed light on an earlier question about the lottery. It sets up the case here and gives רבי עקיבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור, the lot for ה׳ was supposed to be placed on the goat on the כהן גדול's right side. The students ask what to do when the 'לה׳' lot came up in his left hand: may he switch it over? How רבי עקיבא answers will show how strict the rules of the הגרלה are.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Come and hear': introduces a source brought as proof
The lottery that picks which goat is for ה׳ and which is for עזאזל
It came up in the left hand
'May he switch back?': asks whether the move is allowed

phrases.english: Come and hear:
His students asked Rabbi Akiva:
If [the lot for ה׳] came up in the left hand,
what is the law: may he switch it to the right?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון discussion and brings a proof for an earlier question about the הגרלה.
steps.raayaObject: The earlier question about the rules of the הגרלה: whether the lottery is מעכב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording a question put to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: Do not give heretics an opening
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that switching the lot would give the מינין a chance to attack.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Do not give the heretics an opening to dominate.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers his students. He discourages switching the lot because it would give heretics ammunition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים allowed the lot to be moved, the מינין could claim that the rules of the עבודה are not fixed and the חכמים change them as they like. So רבי עקיבא says not to switch. The גמרא will next work out what this implies for its question.

keyTerms.meaning: Heretics who rejected the authority of the חכמים
To dominate, to gain the upper hand
'Do not give a place': do not give an opening

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא's reason is not that the switch fails on its own terms. His concern is how it would look to heretics. Keep this in mind when the גמרא draws its proof from his answer.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Do not give the heretics an opening to dominate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: אַל תִּתְּנוּ מָקוֹם לַמִּינִין לִרְדּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question from step 6, giving the content of the proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Do not switch the lot, so as not to give the מינין grounds to claim the rules are flexible.

steps.title: Inference from רבי עקיבא's reason: the lot could be switched
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רבי עקיבא's reason ('don't give the מינין a chance') that, without that worry, the lot could be switched. That suggests the הגרלה does not really fix the goats' roles, so it is not מעכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The only reason he refused was 'don't give the heretics a chance to attack.' That means that otherwise we would switch the lot! But you said the lottery is indispensable. Once the left hand has fixed it, how could we switch it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at רבי עקיבא's answer. It argues that his answer implies the lot could be switched, which clashes with the idea that the הגרלה is מעכב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא gave only an outside reason (the מינין) for not switching. That suggests that, by itself, switching would be allowed. If the lottery truly decided which goat is for ה' and which is for עזאזל, you could never switch it, so the הגרלה must not be מעכב.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason (here: the ONLY reason given)
But if not for this (reason)
We would return / switch it
The lottery is indispensable (without it the עבודה is invalid)
It (the left hand) has fixed / designated it

phrases.english: The reason is 'do not give an opportunity'
to the heretics to dominate
which implies that if not for this
we would switch it
phrases.notes: Switch the lot to the right hand.

phrases.english: But didn't you say the lottery is indispensable?
And once the left hand has fixed it
how could we switch it?

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּאַל תִּתְּנוּ מָקוֹם לַמִּינִין לִרְדּוֹת, הָא לָאו הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from רבי עקיבא's answer in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the הגרלה is not מעכב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The implication of רבי עקיבא's answer: the only obstacle to switching the lot is the מינין.

steps.title: רבא: the question was only about moving the lot and goat to the right side
steps.stepSummary: רבא rereads the question to רבי עקיבא. They asked whether the lot, together with its own goat, could be moved to the right side. Nobody suggested changing which goat is for ה'. So there is no proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is what they were asking. The lot came up in the left hand. May they move it, together with its goat, to the right side? He told them: Do not give the heretics a chance to attack.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes away the proof from step 8. He explains that the question never involved switching the goats' roles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the new reading, the goat that was chosen for ה' stays the goat for ה'. It is only moved physically to the right side, because the right side is more honored. Since the designation never changes, nothing here shows that the הגרלה is not מעכב.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what they are saying (a re-reading of the question)
And its (own) goat
Right side

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does NOT mean switching which goat goes to ה'. The same goat keeps the same role. It is only moved from the left side to the right side.

phrases.english: Rava said: this is what they are saying:
If the lot came up in the left hand,
what is the law? May they move it
and its goat to the right side?
He said to them:
Do not give the heretics an opportunity to dominate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 8 by redefining the case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from רבי עקיבא's answer.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumed the question was about changing the designation. It was only about the physical position of the lot and its own goat.

steps.title: New proof: once the lot came up, it need not be placed on the goat
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא reads the word 'עלה' (came up) in the פסוק. Once the lot has come up, there is no need to physically place it on the goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If the פסוק had said only 'the goat upon which,' I would have said he must place the lot on it. So the פסוק says 'came up.' Once it came up, nothing more is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof, a ברייתא about the lot and the goat. This step only states the ברייתא; the next steps will work out what it proves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא contrasts two readings. 'עליו' (upon it) would suggest placing the lot on the goat. 'עלה' (came up) shows that the coming-up of the lot is the key act. After that, physically placing it is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: If it had said
He shall place it
The verse teaches (by saying)
It came up (the lot)
It is no longer necessary

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If the verse had said:
'The goat upon which,'
I would say he must place it upon it,
therefore the verse says: 'came up,'
once it has come up
nothing more is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a new proof is brought.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on the פסוק 'אשר עלה עליו הגורל' (ויקרא טז:ט).

steps.title: What does 'not necessary' mean? It cannot mean 'not even a מצוה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what sense placing the lot is 'not necessary.' It cannot mean that placing is not even a מצוה, since placing is clearly part of the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what is it 'not necessary'? If you say it is not needed even as a מצוה, that would mean placing the lot is not even a מצוה at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by 'not necessary.' It rules out the first option and sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways something can be 'not necessary': not even a מצוה, or not מעכב. The first option is rejected, because placing the lot is surely at least a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: For what (purpose)? In what sense?
If you say
As a מצוה (the ideal way of doing it)
By implication
Placing (the lot on the goat)

phrases.english: For what?
If you say: not even as a מצוה,
that would imply placing is not even a מצוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the phrase 'שוב אינו צריך' from the ברייתא in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what sense is placing the lot 'not necessary': as a מצוה, or as a requirement that is מעכב?

steps.title: Proposed proof: the lottery is indispensable, placing the lot is not
steps.stepSummary: 'Not necessary' must mean 'not מעכב.' So the הגרלה is מעכב, while the הנחה is only a מצוה and not מעכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must mean it is not indispensable. Learn from this: the lottery is indispensable, but placing the lot is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the only remaining reading of the ברייתא and draws the conclusion about the lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the placing is called 'not necessary.' That implies the coming-up of the lot, the הגרלה itself, IS necessary in the strict sense. So the הגרלה is מעכב.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that
Regarding being indispensable (invalidating if missing)
And learn from it

steps.whatToRemember: There are two levels: מצוה (the ideal way) and מעכב (required for validity). This step tries to prove from the ברייתא that the הגרלה is מעכב and the הנחה is not. רבא rejects this proof in the next step, so it is not the final word.
steps.whyThisMatters: This would settle the question of the סוגיא, but רבא rejects the proof in the next step. The גמרא then has to bring yet another source (step 14).

phrases.english: Rather, is it not about being indispensable?
And learn from it:
the lottery is indispensable,
placing the lot is not indispensable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the only remaining reading after step 11 ruled out the first option, and concludes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the הגרלה is מעכב while the הנחה is not.

steps.title: רבא: the lot only needs to touch the goat for a moment
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the ברייתא on 'עלה' is not about whether the הנחה is מעכב. It only teaches that the lot does not have to stay on the goat until שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is what the ברייתא means. If the פסוק had only said 'אשר עליו' (upon which), I would think the כהן must leave the lot on the goat until it is slaughtered. So the פסוק says 'אשר עלה' (which came up). Once the lot has come up and been placed, nothing more is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the previous proof by giving a different meaning to the ברייתא's phrase 'not necessary.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, 'אינו צריך' was read as 'placing the lot is not מעכב.' רבא reads it as 'the lot does not need to stay on the goat until שחיטה.' On his reading, the ברייתא never discusses whether placing the lot is essential, so it proves nothing either way.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who often rereads a source to reject a proof
'This is what it means.' It introduces a new reading of a source
'Had it said.' It shows what we would think without a certain word
The time of slaughtering
'The פסוק teaches.' It brings the word in the פסוק that settles the point

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is saying placing the lot does not matter. He only says this ברייתא is about how LONG the lot stays on the goat, not about whether placing it is essential.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is what it is saying:
If it had said 'upon which,'
I would have said he must leave it on the goat
until the time of slaughter.
So the verse says: 'which came up,'
phrases.notes: Here the word עלה is read as 'came up' out of the box.

phrases.english: once it has come up, nothing more is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion drawn in steps 10 to 12 by rereading 'אינו צריך.'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the 'עלה' ברייתא about whether the הנחה or הגרלה is מעכב
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Not necessary' refers to keeping the lot on the goat until שחיטה, not to whether it is מעכב.

steps.title: New proof: only the lot makes the goat a sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads 'ועשהו חטאת' as saying that only the גורל, and not a verbal naming, makes the goat a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And he shall make it a חטאת.' This teaches that the lot makes it a חטאת. Calling it by the name 'חטאת' does not make it a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new proof with תא שמע. It quotes a ברייתא showing that the lot is what gives the goat its status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only the גורל can make the goat a חטאת, then without a lottery the goat never gets its role. That points toward the הגרלה being מעכב. The ברייתא now goes on to explain why a פסוק was needed for this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Come and hear.' It introduces a new source as a proof
'And he shall make it a sin-offering' (ויקרא ט״ז:ט׳)
The lot
The name, meaning saying out loud 'this is a חטאת'

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key source for the idea that the lottery itself creates the goat's identity. That is why skipping it could make the עבודה invalid.

phrases.english: Come and hear: 'And he shall make it a sin-offering,'
the lot makes it a sin-offering,
and the name does not make it a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the last proof was rejected, a new source is brought.
steps.raayaObject: That the הגרלה is essential for making the goat a חטאת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא ט״ז:ט׳, 'ועשהו חטאת'

steps.title: The ברייתא's logical argument that naming should also work
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a קל וחומר. In other cases, naming makes an animal holy even though a lottery does not. So here, where a lottery does work, naming should surely work too.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might have thought otherwise. Isn't it logical? In a case where a lottery does not make an animal holy (like a יולדת's birds), naming it does. So in a case where a lottery does make it holy, shouldn't naming surely work too?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, we see the 'I might have thought' reasoning. It explains why the פסוק was needed. This step sets up the ברייתא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is this: naming works even where lotteries are useless. So naming should be at least as strong where lotteries do work. If that were true, the goat could be designated by naming it, and the lottery would not be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I might have thought.' It introduces a mistaken assumption
'Is it not logical?' It opens a קל וחומר
Made holy, gave the animal its designated status
An argument from a weaker case to a stronger one

phrases.english: For I might have thought: is it not logical?
If, in a place where the lot does not consecrate,
phrases.notes: For example, the two birds a יולדת brings.

phrases.english: the name does consecrate,
then in a place where the lot does consecrate,

steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that only the גורל can make the goat a חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: naming works even where a lottery does not, so it should surely work where a lottery does.

steps.title: The verse overrides the logic: only the lot works
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers the קל וחומר with the פסוק 'ועשהו חטאת.' Only the lot makes the goat a חטאת, not the name.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק says, 'And he shall make it a חטאת.' The lot makes it a חטאת. The name does not make it a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects its own קל וחומר by pointing to the פסוק. For these goats, only the lottery counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר would let naming replace the lottery. The פסוק blocks that. It teaches that for the שעירי יום הכיפורים, the goats get their roles only through the גורל. The גמרא will next look at what this ברייתא tells us about whether the הגרלה is מעכב.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes, meaning it creates the goat's status
The two goats of יום הכיפורים

steps.whatToRemember: For the יום הכיפורים goats, only the גורל gives the goat its status as a חטאת. Simply naming it does not work, even though a קל וחומר might suggest it should.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Naming the goat a חטאת should work, by a קל וחומר from cases where naming works but lotteries do not.
